title: Seamark trace v1
description: What an agent did, in one shape whatever observed it. The capture level on every event is what decides what the document may claim: a trace read from the agent's own transcript cannot assert authenticity, and says so rather than leaving the field out. Field names follow the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions where those have one. Arguments and results travel as sha256 digests, because these files hold somebody's conversation; the literal content appears only when the caller asked for it. Nothing here is a summary and nothing here is a number standing in for evidence.

session_id.description: The session this trace is about, as the source names it.

source.description: What produced the trace: an agent's own transcript reader, or a proxy.

versions.description: Every version of the agent that wrote part of the bytes this trace was derived from. A list rather than one string because the format is the agent's internal one and it changes between releases.

state.description: not_evaluated means the question does not apply at this capture level, which is the L0 case: the audited agent wrote the transcript itself. not_established means it applied and could not be answered, which is a failure. The two are kept apart because conflating them is how a tool ends up claiming what it never observed.

applies.description: Whether the capture level is one at which authenticity is a question at all.

complete.description: True only when something recorded that the session ended AND nothing recorded a hole. Failure is the default: an absence of bad news is not good news. A capture level whose format has no end-of-session record therefore never produces a complete trace, and says so in an `end_not_recorded` hole rather than assuming the file was finished.

child_returncode.description: The exit code of the watched command, when there was one. Deliberately not part of completeness: a trace of a failed run is a complete trace of a failed run.

gaps.description: Everything that happened and was not observed, with where in the order it sits and why.

blind_spots.description: What this capture level cannot see at all, declared by the level rather than inferred per session. A question outside the level is unanswerable, never answered False.

duplicate_records_collapsed.description: How many records the source wrote for a call it had already recorded, collapsed onto the one event that call is. A fact about the source that this document does not otherwise carry, because the collapsed records are not in it. Absent means nobody counted, which is not zero.

capture_level.description: L0 the agent's own transcript; L1 an MCP proxy; L2 a network proxy; L3 a seccomp sandbox. L2 and L3 are named so a rule can refuse by name before they exist.

index.description: Position in this document, consecutive from zero. What a non-conformance cites.

result_sha256.description: Null means the result was never recorded, which is a gap, and not that the result was empty.

error.type.description: Set when the tool itself reported a failure. An observed failure is not a missing observation.

sidechain.description: Whether the call came from a sub-agent of the same session.

gen_ai.tool.call.arguments.description: The literal arguments. Present only when the caller explicitly asked to keep content.

gen_ai.tool.call.result.description: The literal result. Present only when the caller explicitly asked to keep content.

after_index.description: Where `after_event` sits in this document's events. Present only when the identity resolves to exactly one event here; otherwise `after_index_absent` is present instead. Never -1: a hole before every event has no index, it has a reason.

reason.description: A closed vocabulary. An open one is how `unknown` becomes the commonest value.

after_event.description: The `gen_ai.tool.call.id` of the event this hole sits after. Absent when the hole is not attributable to a position between two observed events.

after_index_absent.description: Why this hole cites no position. Present exactly when `after_index` is not, so a consumer can never read a missing anchor as position zero.

gap.description: A hole, anchored to the IDENTITY of the event it follows rather than to a position. The position is resolved against this document's events when the document is written, so it cannot go stale when the events are ordered; when there is no event to anchor to, `after_index` is ABSENT and `after_index_absent` says why. An invented position is indistinguishable from a measured one.
